title: Melville-to-St. Francisville nitrate ratios were 19% higher in summer after flow adjustment in matched 1980-2025 samples
abstract: We tested whether the Atchafalaya-to-Mississippi nitrate concentration ratio was lower in summer after flow adjustment. We used USGS release 3.0 and matched Melville with St. Francisville samples within seven days. The test kept 247 pairs from 40 calendar years in 1980-2025. A model with year effects and quadratic terms for total flow and flow ratio gave an 18.63% higher summer concentration ratio. The conditional 95% three-year block interval was 6.72% to 35.67%. Thus, the contrast had the opposite sign to the starting hypothesis. All planned matching and flow checks gave positive contrasts. The estimate was smaller in 2003-2025 than in 1980-2002; we did not test a period change. Source mixing, travel lag, sparse samples and measurement changes limit inference. These sites are not an inlet and outlet around the whole Atchafalaya floodplain. The result cannot establish nitrate removal or a physical cause. Public-domain inputs, source hashes, code, all pairs, resampling evidence, an independent audit and a static figure are included.

display.caption: Observed Melville-to-St. Francisville nitrate plus nitrite concentration ratios and all planned summer contrasts. Intervals use three-year blocks and condition on the sampled record. The primary test used 247 pairs in 40 years. Concentration differences do not establish nitrogen removal.
